problem: Find the signed curvature of the curve $y=x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ at $x=\pi .$
worked_solution:
The signed curvature $k(x)$ of a plane curve $y=y(x)$ is given by

$$
k(x)=\frac{{y}^{″}(x)}{(1+[{y}^{′}(x)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

First, we calculate ${y}^{′}(x)$ and ${y}^{″}(x):$

$$
{y}^{′}(x)=1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x,\,{y}^{″}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the signed curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}k(x) & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{{[1+{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}^{2}]}^{3/2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curvature at $x=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}k(0) & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{{[1+{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ))}^{2}]}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{{2}^{3/2}} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
